question: How far off is a stage-weighted pipeline forecast of a quarter's wins when its stage probabilities are a CRM's defaults, learned from history, or depend on time in stage; and how long from signed to live?

data.source: CanadaBuys open data, Government of Canada
data.cutoff: the download date; the latest publication date in the tender file is recorded in results
data.dropped_fields: contact names, emails, phones, fax and addresses are never loaded

opportunity.expected_start: expected contract start date of the latest-published notice
opportunity.cancelled_at: for a notice with status Cancelled, its amendment date (else its closing date)
opportunity.won_at: min contract award date over award rows with amendment type Original or blank and award date >= created_at
opportunity.won_known_at: min publication date over those award rows
opportunity.amount: sum of contract amounts above 1 over those rows; missing when none
opportunity.go_live_at: min contract start date over those rows

channel_groups.Other: every other notice type, including blank

stages_at_snapshot.days_in_stage: S - created_at (open for bids), S - bid_close_at (awaiting award)

target: count of pipeline-at-S opportunities with won_at in [S, next quarter start), using all awards published up to the cutoff

fixed.date_rule: expected close date in [S, quarter end): expected_start when present, else bid_close_at
fixed.source_of_weights: HubSpot default deal pipeline: Presentation scheduled 60%, Decision maker bought-in 80% (40/60 and 80/90 are the neighbouring default stages)

learned_stage.weight: share won within the following quarter among history deals in the stage that met the date rule, awards published before S

time_in_stage.weight: share won within the following quarter among history deals in the same stage and band, awards published before S; a cell with fewer than 20 history deals falls back to the stage's pooled share

run_rate.forecast: previous quarter's pipeline-win count, awards published before S

leakage_contrast: learned_stage, time_in_stage and run_rate recomputed with awards published up to the cutoff
interval: 80%: forecast +/- 1.2816 * sqrt(sum p(1-p)), arms fixed, learned_stage, time_in_stage

description_only.go_live: go_live_at - won_at for wins with won_at in [2022-08-08, 2025-09-30]: median, quartiles, share < 0, share >= 30; go_live_at - expected_start where present
description_only.segments: by channel and by the 8 largest departments (names normalised for spelling variants): opportunities created 2022-08-08 to 2025-06-30, win rate, median days created to won, share cancelled
description_only.amounts: share of wins with a usable amount; median amount

stopping_rule: every arm on every snapshot, all published; nothing tuned after results
